title: Differentiation and protecting what is yours
audience: Yoga, Pilates and personal or group fitness teachers who are launching a named class, program or written material, and who want to stand apart from other teachers in their area.
learningOutcomes: Name three points of difference for a teaching offer, each tied to a practice the teacher actually delivers
Distinguish a general idea or style that others can use from a specific name or created material that may be protectable, and check the Australian position before relying on it.
Run a name check and a differentiation check before a new class or program name is published

instruction.heading: Differentiation is a choice a client can point to
instruction.body: A class timetable often looks much the same from one suburb to the next. Differentiation means a client can point to one thing another teacher does not offer, and that thing matters to them. Good points of difference are concrete: the size of the group, a plan for people who are new to exercise, the time of day, a setting such as a beach or a park, a clear progression across weeks, a community of regulars, or a method of feedback. Weak points are labels with nothing behind them. Write three points of difference, and for each one name the part of the class where a client will see or feel it. If you cannot name that moment, the point is not yet a difference you can deliver.

instruction.heading: Separating ideas from things you can own
instruction.body: Ideas, general styles and common poses are not owned by any one person. Anyone can teach a sequence of standing poses, combine two approaches, or teach at dawn. A specific brand name, a logo, a written program with its own wording, or recorded material you created may be capable of protection, depending on its form and how it is used. Check the current guidance from the national intellectual property office and take advice from a qualified IP adviser before you file, rely on protection, or raise a complaint against another teacher. Overseas cases in which teachers have tried to protect a fixed class format have drawn public opposition. Those cases are historical and non-Australian, and they do not establish any Australian position.

instruction.heading: Checking a name before you commit to it
instruction.body: Before a new class name appears on a website, a timetable or a flyer, run a name check. Search the public trademark register, search business names and domain names, and search the websites and social profiles of teachers in your area and online. Look for names that sound like yours, share its key word, or describe the same offer in a way that could confuse a client. A name that simply describes what the class is, rather than distinguishing it, is usually harder to own. Record each search, its date and its result. If a conflict is possible, take advice before launch, because changing a name after signs are printed is expensive.

instruction.heading: Keeping a record of what you created
instruction.body: If you write a course outline, a written program, a set of cueing notes or a recorded class, keep dated drafts and a note of who wrote each part. This record shows what you made and when. It is still good practice. It lets you explain how a class was built, it helps when a colleague you worked with later disputes a shared program, and it reduces the risk of reusing another teacher's written material by accident. Where you use shared material from someone else, get their written permission and keep it on file with {{business:compliance.policy_reference}}.

procedure: List three points of difference and name the moment in the class where each one shows
Write each point as a sentence a client could repeat to a friend
Sort every class name and program name you are considering into one of three groups: idea, general term or specific name
For each specific name, run a public trademark register search, a business name search, a domain search and a social profile search
Record each search, its date and its result
Where a conflict is possible, stop and take advice before the name is published
Keep dated drafts of any written program or recorded material, with the author noted

workedExamples.situation: A fictional teacher, Priya, wants to launch a name for her morning vinyasa-style class in a Wollongong park. A studio two suburbs away already uses a similar word for its weekend retreat programs.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should Priya publish the name now, and what should she check first?
workedExamples.reasoning: She should not publish yet. The similar word appears in another business, which means a possible conflict that needs checking and, if the search is unclear, advice. She should also see whether the other words in the name are general terms, which are harder to own. Her stronger route is a distinctive name, supported by her own points of difference such as the outdoor setting, the group size and a beginner route. She should keep a record of each search and its result before the name appears anywhere.

workedExamples.situation: A fictional Pilates instructor, Marco, has written a twelve-week program that includes his own cueing notes and sequence design. A former colleague asks to copy the document for a new studio.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should Marco check before he agrees, and what record should he already have?
workedExamples.reasoning: Marco should check his own dated drafts and any earlier agreement about the shared work before he replies. He should already have the dated drafts and a note of which parts he wrote. Agreeing in writing, with clear terms about use and credit, is the safer step.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE is required for this lesson
A record for the name checks, with a place for the date, the source checked and the result
A dated drafts folder for any written program or recorded material
A written list of points of difference, each with its class moment

commonErrors.error: Treating every common pose sequence as something one teacher owns
commonErrors.prevention: Sort ideas from specific expression. Protect only your specific expression, and only if the law allows it.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a class name before any search has been run
commonErrors.prevention: Run the name check and record it before the name appears on any channel, including social media.

commonErrors.error: Using another teacher's program wording without permission
commonErrors.prevention: Write your own wording from your own experience. Get written permission before using any shared material.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Nothing here is legal advice. Take advice from a qualified adviser before you rely on any form of protection.
Overseas patent and trademark cases over class formats are historical and non-Australian. They are not evidence of any Australian position.

qualityStandard: Each point of difference is tied to a named moment in a real class
Each specific name has a recorded search, with its date and its result
No published name or program wording is copied from another teacher
documentationEvidence: Points of difference, with the class moment for each
Name search record, with the date, the sources checked and the result
Dated drafts of any written program, with author notes
Written permission for any shared material used
summary: A difference is real only when a client can see it in the class
Ideas and general terms are usually shared.
Search before you publish, and keep a record of the search
Keep dated drafts so you can show what you made and when

knowledgeChecks.question: Which is the strongest point of difference for a yoga or fitness offer?
options: A label that says the class is premium and that the price is set high on purpose
A sentence that says the teacher is the best in the area and that the studio is well known
A named outdoor setting and a small group size that a client sees in every session

knowledgeChecks.question: A teacher wants to name a class with a general word that describes what the class does. What does this lesson say about that kind of word?
options: A descriptive word is usually harder to own, and whether it can be registered in Australia has not yet been confirmed
Any general word is protected in Australia as soon as it is used and it needs no search or registration at all
A general word is the easiest kind to own, so no check is needed and the teacher can use it on any sign

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen before a specific class name is published?
options: The name should be printed on signs so that it is fixed before any search is run
A name search should be run and recorded, and any possible conflict taken to advice
The name should be used on social media for a month first to see how it is received
